content.title: At Coachella, Justin Bieber spends half an hour surfing YouTube
content.text: INDIO, Calif. — This was not the Justin Bieber the world remembered. It was probably not the Justin Bieber they wanted, either. Each year, Coachella has three headliners. But unofficially, the Canadian popstar was the Indio festival’s main act. It seems hardly a coincidence that 2026, the year of Bieber’s return, was the first year that Coachella had quickly sold out since 2022. This was “Bieberchella.” Three years after retreating from the spotlight, his Saturday night set was set to be his biggest performance in years. What fans hoped for, it seems, was vintage Bieber. They wanted the hits: “Baby,” “One Less Lonely Girl,” “Sorry.” They wanted nostalgia; they wanted a dance party. They wanted a pop star with a microphone headset and a flock of backup dancers. They wanted choreography. Article continues below this adBieber had other ideas. Saturday’s 90-minute performance was stubbornly underproduced, so lo-fi that it felt like an overcorrection from his polished career as a teenage star. The singer appeared on stage alone, with a pink hoodie pulled over his head and sunglasses across his eyes. He selected his backing tracks manually from a Mac on the side of the stage. Occasionally, he scrolled through comments on the Coachella livestream to pick his next songs.“I was thinking maybe you guys could help me with the songs tonight, maybe help pick the favorites,” he explained, sharing the livestream’s comments to the screens on the stage. Make SFGATE a preferred source so your search results prioritize writing by actual people, not AI.Add Preferred SourceThose favorites apparently excluded his old material. The singer played only snippets of “Baby,” “Never Say Never,” “Beauty and a Beat” and his other early hits. Instead, Bieber pulled mostly from his newest albums, 2025’s “Swag” and “Swag II.” The albums are two discs of stripped-back, lo-fi R&B, a departure from his pop sound. The only other songs he played in full weren’t his own: “Stay” (which Bieber does feature on), with special guest The Kid Laroi; and “Essence,” with Wizkid and Tems. Article continues below this adIt’s clear that this is how Bieber likes it. Some of the “Swag” tracks sounded beautiful live. Bieber’s opener, “All I Can Take,” was an immediate reminder of his voice’s power. (With sunglasses covering his eyes and a hood over his head, there was nothing else to focus on aside from his voice, anyway.) Things got weird a third of the way through the set when Bieber started playing through his old material. Or rather, his computer did. The singer sat perched in front of his Mac, searching for his old music videos on YouTube. He shared his computer’s screen so that the crowd could see. When he clicked on the video for “Baby,” the audience’s reaction was immediate. What had been a quiet crowd jumped to attention. Phones flew up, and fans sang along. Bieber did too, quietly, his new voice an octave lower.And then, after a minute, he pulled the plug. He searched for another song, “Favorite Girl,” and did the same routine: one minute, then on to the next. And so on for “Confident,” “All That Matters” and “Sorry,” among others.Article continues below this ad“Do you really go all the way back?” Bieber kept saying as he searched for the next song. “Like for real for real?”For Bieber, this segment of his set seemed to be less a performance than a trip down memory lane. On some tracks, he let his younger self do the heavy lifting, singing along on every other line. “Sorry to cut it, but these are just little snippets,” he said at another point. “I wanna see how far back you really go.”Article continues below this adFor good measure, he surfed around on YouTube for longer, cycling through some viral videos. Among them, the double rainbow video, Deez Nuts and a clip of his viral “it’s not clocking to you” confrontation with the paparazzi. Bieber has lived a whole lifetime — or several — since he was first plucked from YouTube obscurity. From the days that he sang on the Ellen show or wore a purple hoodie, Bieber has grown up in the spotlight, and stepped into adulthood under the close scrutiny of paparazzi, tabloids and millions of fans. In time, his voice dropped. He got a DUI, covered his body in tattoos, hard-launched as a Christian and left behind his younger image to start singing about sex. He battled substance abuse. He got married and had a son. He transitioned from a teen idol with legions of obsessive fans to an ordinary pop star. Justin Bieber and Tems perform at the Coachella Stage.Kevin Mazur/Getty Images for CoachellaSaturday’s performance was set to be something of a comeback for Bieber. The artist cancelled the remainder of his last tour, the Justice World Tour, in 2023. The cancellation came after Bieber postponed earlier shows in the tour over an unspecified illness, and announced that he had Ramsay Hunt syndrome, a neurological condition that had partially paralyzed his face. The cancellation cost him, according to People: The company of his former manager, Scooter Braun, covered the cost of the cancellation, and as part of a settlement, Bieber reportedly paid Braun back $26 million last year.Article continues below this adIn the years since, the singer has kept quiet. He released no music himself for three years. He sold his entire catalog for $200 million as rumors circulated that his finances were tenuous and that he had replaced his old team with a circle of yes-men. He split with Braun, who had managed him since 2008.In the summer of 2025, Bieber stepped back into the spotlight. “Swag” and “Swag II” are his first standalone projects since 2021’s “Justice.” The albums are produced in part by Dijon, who was a special guest on Saturday. In February, Bieber performed a song shirtless at the Grammys.Considering the evidence presented at Saturday’s Coachella performance — the denied gratification, the hits cut short — one could draw the conclusion that Justin Bieber is trolling his fans.Got a tip? Send us the scoop.DO IT NOW But hearing him sing passionately through “Yukon,” and watching him smile while flipping through his old music videos, it seems that this is just the thing that makes him happy. Justin Bieber wanted an intimate set, something simple to connect him to his fans and his past. Article continues below this adFor some, “intimate” might be a synonym for “boring.” But at least one person had a great time:“I hope you guys drive home safe,” Bieber said, almost timidly, before signing off. “Drink some water. I loved spending this time with you guys.”Justin Bieber, draped in black, waves to the crowd from the Coachella Stage.Kevin Mazur/Getty Images for CoachellaApril 12, 2026Timothy Karoff is SFGATE’s culture reporter.
